name: BASIC
note: Designed at Dartmouth to make computing accessible to students outside computer science
typeSystem: Dialect-dependent and generally loose. Original Dartmouth BASIC used undeclared numeric variables; later dialects added strings and often used suffixes such as $ or % to indicate a type.
runtime: Original Dartmouth BASIC used a fast compile-and-go system. Many later microcomputer dialects, including Microsoft BASIC and Applesoft BASIC, used interactive line-oriented interpreters that often shipped in ROM.

runtimes.name: Dartmouth compile-and-go system
runtimes.role: The original 1964 implementation compiled a submitted program and then ran it with quick turnaround on the time-sharing system.

runtimes.name: Line interpreter (e.g. Microsoft BASIC, Applesoft BASIC)
runtimes.role: Reads and executes numbered programs interactively; the dominant execution model on many 1970s-80s home computers.

compilers.name: Dartmouth BASIC compiler
compilers.role: The original compile-and-go implementation for the Dartmouth Time-Sharing System.

concurrencyModel: N/A in the original and typical home-computer dialects; programs normally execute sequentially.
